items.text:
विश्वं विष्णुर्वषट्कारो भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुः।
भूतकृद्भूतभृद्भावो भूतात्मा भूतभावनः॥१॥
items.tr:
viśvaṃ viṣṇurvaṣaṭkāro bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhuḥ|
bhūtakṛdbhūtabhṛdbhāvo bhūtātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ||1||
items.en: He is the universe (Vishva), the all-pervading one (Vishnu), the one invoked in sacrifice (Vashatkara), the lord of past, future and present (Bhutabhavyabhavatprabhu), the maker of beings (Bhutakrit), their supporter (Bhutabhrit), pure existence (Bhava), the self of all beings (Bhutatma) and the one who brings them forth (Bhutabhavana).

items.text:
पूतात्मा परमात्मा च मुक्तानां परमा गतिः।
अव्ययः पुरुषः साक्षी क्षेत्रज्ञोऽक्षर एव च॥२॥
items.tr:
pūtātmā paramātmā ca muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ|
avyayaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣī kṣetrajño'kṣara eva ca||2||
items.en: He is the pure Self (Putatma), the Supreme Self (Paramatma), the highest goal of the freed (Muktanam Parama Gati), the undying one (Avyaya), the Person (Purusha), the witness (Sakshi), the knower of the field (Kshetrajna) and the imperishable (Akshara).

items.text:
योगो योगविदां नेता प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः।
नारसिंहवपुः श्रीमान् केशवः पुरुषोत्तमः॥३॥
items.tr:
yogo yogavidāṃ netā pradhānapuruṣeśvaraḥ|
nārasiṃhavapuḥ śrīmān keśavaḥ puruṣottamaḥ||3||
items.en: He is union (Yoga), the guide of those who know yoga (Yogavidam Neta), the lord of nature and spirit (Pradhanapurusheshvara), the one in the man-lion form (Narasimhavapu), the glorious one (Shriman), the fair-haired one (Keshava) and the Supreme Person (Purushottama).

items.text:
सर्वः शर्वः शिवः स्थाणुर्भूतादिर्निधिरव्ययः।
संभवो भावनो भर्ता प्रभवः प्रभुरीश्वरः॥४॥
items.tr:
sarvaḥ śarvaḥ śivaḥ sthāṇurbhūtādirnidhiravyayaḥ|
saṃbhavo bhāvano bhartā prabhavaḥ prabhurīśvaraḥ||4||
items.en: He is everything (Sarva), the destroyer (Sharva), the auspicious one (Shiva), the unmoving (Sthanu), the source of beings (Bhutadi), the undying treasure (Nidhir Avyaya), the one who appears by his own will (Sambhava), the giver of life (Bhavana), the sustainer (Bharta), the origin (Prabhava), the master (Prabhu) and the ruler (Ishvara).

items.text:
स्वयंभूः शम्भुरादित्यः पुष्कराक्षो महास्वनः।
अनादिनिधनो धाता विधाता धातुरुत्तमः॥५॥
items.tr:
svayaṃbhūḥ śambhurādityaḥ puṣkarākṣo mahāsvanaḥ|
anādinidhano dhātā vidhātā dhāturuttamaḥ||5||
items.en: He is self-born (Svayambhu), the giver of joy (Shambhu), the son of Aditi (Aditya), the lotus-eyed (Pushkaraksha), the one with a mighty voice (Mahasvana), without beginning or end (Anadinidhana), the upholder (Dhata), the arranger (Vidhata) and the highest element (Dhaturuttama).

items.text:
अप्रमेयो हृषीकेशः पद्मनाभोऽमरप्रभुः।
विश्वकर्मा मनुस्त्वष्टा स्थविष्ठः स्थविरो ध्रुवः॥६॥
items.tr:
aprameyo hṛṣīkeśaḥ padmanābho'maraprabhuḥ|
viśvakarmā manustvaṣṭā sthaviṣṭhaḥ sthaviro dhruvaḥ||6||
items.en: He is beyond measure (Aprameya), the lord of the senses (Hrishikesha), lotus-navelled (Padmanabha), lord of the immortals (Amaraprabhu), maker of the universe (Vishvakarma), the thinker (Manu), the shaper (Tvashta), the most massive (Sthavishtha), the ancient (Sthavira) and the steady one (Dhruva).

items.text:
अग्राह्यः शाश्वतः कृष्णो लोहिताक्षः प्रतर्दनः।
प्रभूतस्त्रिककुब्धाम पवित्रं मङ्गलं परम्॥७॥
items.tr:
agrāhyaḥ śāśvataḥ kṛṣṇo lohitākṣaḥ pratardanaḥ|
prabhūtastrikakubdhāma pavitraṃ maṅgalaṃ param||7||
items.en: He cannot be grasped (Agrahya), is eternal (Shashvata), dark and all-attracting (Krishna), red-eyed (Lohitaksha), the destroyer (Pratardana), full of all wealth (Prabhuta), the abode of the three regions (Trikakubdhama), the purifier (Pavitra) and the highest blessing (Mangalam Param).

items.text:
ईशानः प्राणदः प्राणो ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठः प्रजापतिः।
हिरण्यगर्भो भूगर्भो माधवो मधुसूदनः॥८॥
items.tr:
īśānaḥ prāṇadaḥ prāṇo jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prajāpatiḥ|
hiraṇyagarbho bhūgarbho mādhavo madhusūdanaḥ||8||
items.en: He is the ruler (Ishana), the giver of breath (Pranada), breath itself (Prana), the eldest (Jyeshtha), the best (Shreshtha), the lord of creatures (Prajapati), the golden womb (Hiranyagarbha), the one who holds the earth within (Bhugarbha), the husband of Lakshmi (Madhava) and the slayer of the demon Madhu (Madhusudana).

items.text:
ईश्वरो विक्रमी धन्वी मेधावी विक्रमः क्रमः।
अनुत्तमो दुराधर्षः कृतज्ञः कृतिरात्मवान्॥९॥
items.tr:
īśvaro vikramī dhanvī medhāvī vikramaḥ kramaḥ|
anuttamo durādharṣaḥ kṛtajñaḥ kṛtirātmavān||9||
items.en: He is the Lord (Ishvara), the valiant (Vikrami), the archer (Dhanvi), the wise (Medhavi), the one of mighty strides (Vikrama), the one who pervades (Krama), the unsurpassed (Anuttama), the one none can overcome (Duradharsha), the one who remembers good deeds (Kritajna), action itself (Kriti) and the master of himself (Atmavan).

items.text:
सुरेशः शरणं शर्म विश्वरेताः प्रजाभवः।
अहः संवत्सरो व्यालः प्रत्ययः सर्वदर्शनः॥१०॥
items.tr:
sureśaḥ śaraṇaṃ śarma viśvaretāḥ prajābhavaḥ|
ahaḥ saṃvatsaro vyālaḥ pratyayaḥ sarvadarśanaḥ||10||
items.en: He is lord of the gods (Suresha), the refuge (Sharana), bliss (Sharma), the seed of the universe (Vishvareta), the source of creatures (Prajabhava), the day (Aha), the year (Samvatsara), the one hard to catch, like a serpent (Vyala), trust (Pratyaya) and the one who sees all (Sarvadarshana).

items.text:
अजः सर्वेश्वरः सिद्धः सिद्धिः सर्वादिरच्युतः।
वृषाकपिरमेयात्मा सर्वयोगविनिःसृतः॥११॥
items.tr:
ajaḥ sarveśvaraḥ siddhaḥ siddhiḥ sarvādiracyutaḥ|
vṛṣākapirameyātmā sarvayogaviniḥsṛtaḥ||11||
items.en: He is unborn (Aja), lord of all (Sarveshvara), the perfect one (Siddha), success itself (Siddhi), the beginning of all (Sarvadi), the one who never falls (Achyuta), the lord who is dharma and Varaha (Vrishakapi), of immeasurable nature (Ameyatma) and the one reached through every path of yoga (Sarvayogavinihsrita).

items.text:
वसुर्वसुमनाः सत्यः समात्माऽसम्मितः समः।
अमोघः पुण्डरीकाक्षो वृषकर्मा वृषाकृतिः॥१२॥
items.tr:
vasurvasumanāḥ satyaḥ samātmā'sammitaḥ samaḥ|
amoghaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣo vṛṣakarmā vṛṣākṛtiḥ||12||
items.en: He is the dweller in all (Vasu), of generous mind (Vasumana), the truth (Satya), the same to all (Samatma), beyond comparison (Asammita), even (Sama), never fruitless (Amogha), lotus-eyed (Pundarikaksha), of righteous deeds (Vrishakarma) and righteousness in form (Vrishakriti).

items.text:
रुद्रो बहुशिरा बभ्रुर्विश्वयोनिः शुचिश्रवाः।
अमृतः शाश्वतः स्थाणुर्वरारोहो महातपाः॥१३॥
items.tr:
rudro bahuśirā babhrurviśvayoniḥ śuciśravāḥ|
amṛtaḥ śāśvataḥ sthāṇurvarāroho mahātapāḥ||13||
items.en: He is the one who makes beings weep at the end (Rudra), many-headed (Bahushira), the supporter of the worlds (Babhru), the source of the universe (Vishvayoni), of pure fame (Shuchishrava), immortal (Amrita), eternal (Shashvata), firm (Sthanu), the excellent goal (Vararoha) and of great austerity (Mahatapa).

items.text:
सर्वगः सर्वविद्भानुर्विष्वक्सेनो जनार्दनः।
वेदो वेदविदव्यङ्गो वेदाङ्गो वेदवित् कविः॥१४॥
items.tr:
sarvagaḥ sarvavidbhānurviṣvakseno janārdanaḥ|
vedo vedavidavyaṅgo vedāṅgo vedavit kaviḥ||14||
items.en: He goes everywhere (Sarvaga), knows all (Sarvavid), is the shining one (Bhanu), whose army goes everywhere (Vishvaksena), who troubles wicked people (Janardana); he is the Veda (Veda), knower of the Veda (Vedavid), complete in all parts (Avyanga), whose limbs are the Vedic sciences (Vedanga), the one who reflects on the Veda (Vedavit) and the seer (Kavi).

items.text:
लोकाध्यक्षः सुराध्यक्षो धर्माध्यक्षः कृताकृतः।
चतुरात्मा चतुर्व्यूहश्चतुर्दंष्ट्रश्चतुर्भुजः॥१५॥
items.tr:
lokādhyakṣaḥ surādhyakṣo dharmādhyakṣaḥ kṛtākṛtaḥ|
caturātmā caturvyūhaścaturdaṃṣṭraścaturbhujaḥ||15||
items.en: He oversees the worlds (Lokadhyaksha), the gods (Suradhyaksha) and dharma (Dharmadhyaksha); he is both effect and cause (Kritakrita), fourfold in self (Chaturatma), in four forms (Chaturvyuha), four-tusked (Chaturdamshtra) and four-armed (Chaturbhuja).

items.text:
भ्राजिष्णुर्भोजनं भोक्ता सहिष्णुर्जगदादिजः।
अनघो विजयो जेता विश्वयोनिः पुनर्वसुः॥१६॥
items.tr:
bhrājiṣṇurbhojanaṃ bhoktā sahiṣṇurjagadādijaḥ|
anagho vijayo jetā viśvayoniḥ punarvasuḥ||16||
items.en: He is radiant (Bhrajishnu), the food (Bhojana) and the eater (Bhokta), the patient one (Sahishnu), first-born in the world (Jagadadija), sinless (Anagha), victory (Vijaya), the conqueror (Jeta), the source of all (Vishvayoni) and the one who dwells again and again in bodies (Punarvasu).

items.text:
उपेन्द्रो वामनः प्रांशुरमोघः शुचिरूर्जितः।
अतीन्द्रः संग्रहः सर्गो धृतात्मा नियमो यमः॥१७॥
items.tr:
upendro vāmanaḥ prāṃśuramoghaḥ śucirūrjitaḥ|
atīndraḥ saṃgrahaḥ sargo dhṛtātmā niyamo yamaḥ||17||
items.en: He is the younger brother of Indra (Upendra), the dwarf (Vamana), the tall one (Pramshu), never fruitless (Amogha), pure (Shuchi), mighty (Urjita), above Indra (Atindra), the one who gathers all in (Sangraha), creation (Sarga), self-controlled (Dhritatma), the rule (Niyama) and the controller (Yama).

items.text:
वेद्यो वैद्यः सदायोगी वीरहा माधवो मधुः।
अतीन्द्रियो महामायो महोत्साहो महाबलः॥१८॥
items.tr:
vedyo vaidyaḥ sadāyogī vīrahā mādhavo madhuḥ|
atīndriyo mahāmāyo mahotsāho mahābalaḥ||18||
items.en: He is the one to be known (Vedya), the healer (Vaidya), ever in yoga (Sadayogi), slayer of demon heroes (Viraha), lord of knowledge (Madhava), sweet like honey (Madhu), beyond the senses (Atindriya), of great illusive power (Mahamaya), of great zeal (Mahotsaha) and of great strength (Mahabala).

items.text:
महाबुद्धिर्महावीर्यो महाशक्तिर्महाद्युतिः।
अनिर्देश्यवपुः श्रीमानमेयात्मा महाद्रिधृक्॥१९॥
items.tr:
mahābuddhirmahāvīryo mahāśaktirmahādyutiḥ|
anirdeśyavapuḥ śrīmānameyātmā mahādridhṛk||19||
items.en: He has great wisdom (Mahabuddhi), great valour (Mahavirya), great power (Mahashakti), great splendour (Mahadyuti), a form that cannot be described (Anirdeshyavapu); he is glorious (Shriman), of immeasurable nature (Ameyatma) and the bearer of the great mountain (Mahadridhrik).

items.text:
महेष्वासो महीभर्ता श्रीनिवासः सतां गतिः।
अनिरुद्धः सुरानन्दो गोविन्दो गोविदां पतिः॥२०॥
items.tr:
maheṣvāso mahībhartā śrīnivāsaḥ satāṃ gatiḥ|
aniruddhaḥ surānando govindo govidāṃ patiḥ||20||
items.en: He is the great archer (Maheshvasa), the supporter of the earth (Mahibharta), the dwelling of Lakshmi (Shrinivasa), the goal of the good (Satam Gati), the unstoppable (Aniruddha), the joy of the gods (Surananda), the protector of cows and finder of the earth (Govinda) and lord of those who know speech (Govidam Pati).

items.text:
मरीचिर्दमनो हंसः सुपर्णो भुजगोत्तमः।
हिरण्यनाभः सुतपाः पद्मनाभः प्रजापतिः॥२१॥
items.tr:
marīcirdamano haṃsaḥ suparṇo bhujagottamaḥ|
hiraṇyanābhaḥ sutapāḥ padmanābhaḥ prajāpatiḥ||21||
items.en: He is a ray of light (Marichi), the tamer (Damana), the swan (Hamsa), the fair-winged bird (Suparna), the best of serpents (Bhujagottama), golden-navelled (Hiranyanabha), of good austerity (Sutapa), lotus-navelled (Padmanabha) and lord of creatures (Prajapati).

items.text:
अमृत्युः सर्वदृक् सिंहः सन्धाता सन्धिमान् स्थिरः।
अजो दुर्मर्षणः शास्ता विश्रुतात्मा सुरारिहा॥२२॥
items.tr:
amṛtyuḥ sarvadṛk siṃhaḥ sandhātā sandhimān sthiraḥ|
ajo durmarṣaṇaḥ śāstā viśrutātmā surārihā||22||
items.en: He is deathless (Amrityu), all-seeing (Sarvadrik), the lion (Simha), the one who joins (Sandhata), the one who is joined (Sandhiman), firm (Sthira), unborn (Aja), unbearable to foes (Durmarshana), the teacher (Shasta), of famous nature (Vishrutatma) and slayer of the gods' enemies (Surariha).

items.text:
गुरुर्गुरुतमो धाम सत्यः सत्यपराक्रमः।
निमिषोऽनिमिषः स्रग्वी वाचस्पतिरुदारधीः॥२३॥
items.tr:
gururgurutamo dhāma satyaḥ satyaparākramaḥ|
nimiṣo'nimiṣaḥ sragvī vācaspatirudāradhīḥ||23||
items.en: He is the teacher (Guru), the greatest teacher (Gurutama), the abode (Dhama), the truth (Satya), of true valour (Satyaparakrama), the one who closes his eyes (Nimisha), the ever-watchful (Animisha), wearer of garlands (Sragvi), lord of speech (Vachaspati) and of noble mind (Udaradhi).

items.text:
अग्रणीर्ग्रामणीः श्रीमान् न्यायो नेता समीरणः।
सहस्रमूर्धा विश्वात्मा सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात्॥२४॥
items.tr:
agraṇīrgrāmaṇīḥ śrīmān nyāyo netā samīraṇaḥ|
sahasramūrdhā viśvātmā sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt||24||
items.en: He is the leader in front (Agrani), the chief of the people (Gramani), glorious (Shriman), justice (Nyaya), the guide (Neta), the moving wind (Samirana), thousand-headed (Sahasramurdha), the soul of the universe (Vishvatma), thousand-eyed (Sahasraksha) and thousand-footed (Sahasrapat).

items.text:
आवर्तनो निवृत्तात्मा संवृतः संप्रमर्दनः।
अहः संवर्तको वह्निरनिलो धरणीधरः॥२५॥
items.tr:
āvartano nivṛttātmā saṃvṛtaḥ saṃpramardanaḥ|
ahaḥ saṃvartako vahniranilo dharaṇīdharaḥ||25||
items.en: He turns the wheel of the world (Avartana), is a self apart from the world (Nivrittatma), is veiled (Samvrita), the crusher (Sampramardana), the day (Aha), the one who brings the world to an end (Samvartaka), fire (Vahni), wind (Anila) and the bearer of the earth (Dharanidhara).

items.text:
सुप्रसादः प्रसन्नात्मा विश्वधृग्विश्वभुग्विभुः।
सत्कर्ता सत्कृतः साधुर्जह्नुर्नारायणो नरः॥२६॥
items.tr:
suprasādaḥ prasannātmā viśvadhṛgviśvabhugvibhuḥ|
satkartā satkṛtaḥ sādhurjahnurnārāyaṇo naraḥ||26||
items.en: He is very gracious (Suprasada), of joyful nature (Prasannatma), the bearer of the universe (Vishvadhrik), the enjoyer of it (Vishvabhuk), all-pervading (Vibhu), the one who honours the good (Satkarta), the one honoured (Satkrita), the good (Sadhu), the one who carries beings away (Jahnu), Narayana and Nara.

items.text:
असंख्येयोऽप्रमेयात्मा विशिष्टः शिष्टकृच्छुचिः।
सिद्धार्थः सिद्धसंकल्पः सिद्धिदः सिद्धिसाधनः॥२७॥
items.tr:
asaṃkhyeyo'prameyātmā viśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭakṛcchuciḥ|
siddhārthaḥ siddhasaṃkalpaḥ siddhidaḥ siddhisādhanaḥ||27||
items.en: He is countless (Asankhyeya), of measureless nature (Aprameyatma), the distinguished (Vishishta), the maker of the disciplined (Shishtakrit), pure (Shuchi), the one whose aims are fulfilled (Siddhartha), whose will is fulfilled (Siddhasankalpa), the giver of success (Siddhida) and the means of success (Siddhisadhana).

items.text:
वृषाही वृषभो विष्णुर्वृषपर्वा वृषोदरः।
वर्धनो वर्धमानश्च विविक्तः श्रुतिसागरः॥२८॥
items.tr:
vṛṣāhī vṛṣabho viṣṇurvṛṣaparvā vṛṣodaraḥ|
vardhano vardhamānaśca viviktaḥ śrutisāgaraḥ||28||
items.en: He is the lord of sacred rites (Vrishahi), the bull (Vrishabha), the all-pervading (Vishnu), the one whose steps are dharma (Vrishaparva), whose belly holds dharma (Vrishodara), the one who makes grow (Vardhana), who grows (Vardhamana), the one apart (Vivikta) and the ocean of the scriptures (Shrutisagara).

items.text:
सुभुजो दुर्धरो वाग्मी महेन्द्रो वसुदो वसुः।
नैकरूपो बृहद्रूपः शिपिविष्टः प्रकाशनः॥२९॥
items.tr:
subhujo durdharo vāgmī mahendro vasudo vasuḥ|
naikarūpo bṛhadrūpaḥ śipiviṣṭaḥ prakāśanaḥ||29||
items.en: He has beautiful arms (Subhuja), is hard to hold (Durdhara), eloquent (Vagmi), the great Indra (Mahendra), the giver of wealth (Vasuda), wealth itself (Vasu), of many forms (Naikarupa), of vast form (Brihadrupa), present in the rays (Shipivishta) and the one who reveals (Prakashana).

items.text:
ओजस्तेजोद्युतिधरः प्रकाशात्मा प्रतापनः।
ऋद्धः स्पष्टाक्षरो मन्त्रश्चन्द्रांशुर्भास्करद्युतिः॥३०॥
items.tr:
ojastejodyutidharaḥ prakāśātmā pratāpanaḥ|
ṛddhaḥ spaṣṭākṣaro mantraścandrāṃśurbhāskaradyutiḥ||30||
items.en: He holds vigour, energy and brilliance (Ojastejodyutidhara), is of shining nature (Prakashatma), the one who burns (Pratapana), the prosperous (Riddha), whose words are clear (Spashtakshara), the sacred mantra (Mantra), the moonbeam (Chandramshu) and the sun's splendour (Bhaskaradyuti).

items.text:
अमृतांशूद्भवो भानुः शशबिन्दुः सुरेश्वरः।
औषधं जगतः सेतुः सत्यधर्मपराक्रमः॥३१॥
items.tr:
amṛtāṃśūdbhavo bhānuḥ śaśabinduḥ sureśvaraḥ|
auṣadhaṃ jagataḥ setuḥ satyadharmaparākramaḥ||31||
items.en: He is the source of the moon (Amritamshudbhava), the sun (Bhanu), the hare-marked moon (Shashabindu), lord of the gods (Sureshvara), the medicine (Aushadham), the bridge of the world (Jagatah Setu) and the one whose acts are true and righteous (Satyadharmaparakrama).

items.text:
भूतभव्यभवन्नाथः पवनः पावनोऽनलः।
कामहा कामकृत्कान्तः कामः कामप्रदः प्रभुः॥३२॥
items.tr:
bhūtabhavyabhavannāthaḥ pavanaḥ pāvano'nalaḥ|
kāmahā kāmakṛtkāntaḥ kāmaḥ kāmapradaḥ prabhuḥ||32||
items.en: He is lord of past, future and present (Bhutabhavyabhavannatha), the wind (Pavana), the purifier (Pavana), fire (Anala), the slayer of desire (Kamaha), the fulfiller of desire (Kamakrit), the lovely one (Kanta), love (Kama), the giver of what is desired (Kamaprada) and the master (Prabhu).

items.text:
युगादिकृद्युगावर्तो नैकमायो महाशनः।
अदृश्यो व्यक्तरूपश्च सहस्रजिदनन्तजित्॥३३॥
items.tr:
yugādikṛdyugāvarto naikamāyo mahāśanaḥ|
adṛśyo vyaktarūpaśca sahasrajidanantajit||33||
items.en: He makes the ages begin (Yugadikrit), turns the cycle of ages (Yugavarta), has many magic powers (Naikamaya), devours all at the end (Mahashana), is invisible (Adrishya), and of visible form (Vyaktarupa); he conquers thousands (Sahasrajit) and the endless (Anantajit).

items.text:
इष्टोऽविशिष्टः शिष्टेष्टः शिखण्डी नहुषो वृषः।
क्रोधहा क्रोधकृत्कर्ता विश्वबाहुर्महीधरः॥३४॥
items.tr:
iṣṭo'viśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭeṣṭaḥ śikhaṇḍī nahuṣo vṛṣaḥ|
krodhahā krodhakṛtkartā viśvabāhurmahīdharaḥ||34||
items.en: He is the beloved (Ishta), the one above difference (Avishishta), dear to the disciplined (Shishteshta), wearer of a peacock feather (Shikhandi), the one who binds (Nahusha), dharma (Vrisha), destroyer of anger (Krodhaha), the one who rouses anger against evil (Krodhakrit), the doer (Karta), the one whose arms are everywhere (Vishvabahu) and bearer of the earth (Mahidhara).

items.text:
अच्युतः प्रथितः प्राणः प्राणदो वासवानुजः।
अपांनिधिरधिष्ठानमप्रमत्तः प्रतिष्ठितः॥३५॥
items.tr:
acyutaḥ prathitaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇado vāsavānujaḥ|
apāṃnidhiradhiṣṭhānamapramattaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ||35||
items.en: He is the one who never falls (Achyuta), the renowned (Prathita), breath (Prana), giver of breath (Pranada), younger brother of Indra (Vasavanuja), the treasure of the waters (Apamnidhi), the foundation (Adhishthana), the ever-alert (Apramatta) and the established one (Pratishthita).

items.text:
स्कन्दः स्कन्दधरो धुर्यो वरदो वायुवाहनः।
वासुदेवो बृहद्भानुरादिदेवः पुरन्दरः॥३६॥
items.tr:
skandaḥ skandadharo dhuryo varado vāyuvāhanaḥ|
vāsudevo bṛhadbhānurādidevaḥ purandaraḥ||36||
items.en: He is the one who flows, like nectar (Skanda), the upholder of the right path (Skandadhara), the bearer of burdens (Dhurya), giver of boons (Varada), the one who drives the winds (Vayuvahana), the dweller in all (Vasudeva), of great light (Brihadbhanu), the first God (Adideva) and the destroyer of cities (Purandara).

items.text:
अशोकस्तारणस्तारः शूरः शौरिर्जनेश्वरः।
अनुकूलः शतावर्तः पद्मी पद्मनिभेक्षणः॥३७॥
items.tr:
aśokastāraṇastāraḥ śūraḥ śaurirjaneśvaraḥ|
anukūlaḥ śatāvartaḥ padmī padmanibhekṣaṇaḥ||37||
items.en: He is free of sorrow (Ashoka), the one who carries across (Tarana), the saviour (Tara), the brave (Shura), the descendant of Shura (Shauri), lord of people (Janeshvara), the kindly (Anukula), the one who came a hundred times (Shatavarta), holder of the lotus (Padmi) and lotus-eyed (Padmanibhekshana).

items.text:
पद्मनाभोऽरविन्दाक्षः पद्मगर्भः शरीरभृत्।
महर्द्धिरृद्धो वृद्धात्मा महाक्षो गरुडध्वजः॥३८॥
items.tr:
padmanābho'ravindākṣaḥ padmagarbhaḥ śarīrabhṛt|
maharddhirṛddho vṛddhātmā mahākṣo garuḍadhvajaḥ||38||
items.en: He is lotus-navelled (Padmanabha), lotus-eyed (Aravindaksha), the one in the heart-lotus (Padmagarbha), bearer of bodies (Sharirabhrit), of great riches (Maharddhi), prosperous (Riddha), the ancient self (Vriddhatma), large-eyed (Mahaksha) and the one with Garuda on his banner (Garudadhvaja).

items.text:
अतुलः शरभो भीमः समयज्ञो हविर्हरिः।
सर्वलक्षणलक्षण्यो लक्ष्मीवान् समितिञ्जयः॥३९॥
items.tr:
atulaḥ śarabho bhīmaḥ samayajño havirhariḥ|
sarvalakṣaṇalakṣaṇyo lakṣmīvān samitiñjayaḥ||39||
items.en: He is matchless (Atula), the one who dwells in bodies (Sharabha), the terrible (Bhima), the knower of right times (Samayajna), the offering (Havirhari), the one with every auspicious mark (Sarvalakshanalakshanya), with Lakshmi (Lakshmivan) and the winner of battles (Samitinjaya).

items.text:
विक्षरो रोहितो मार्गो हेतुर्दामोदरः सहः।
महीधरो महाभागो वेगवानमिताशनः॥४०॥
items.tr:
vikṣaro rohito mārgo heturdāmodaraḥ sahaḥ|
mahīdharo mahābhāgo vegavānamitāśanaḥ||40||
items.en: He is unfading (Vikshara), red (Rohita), the path (Marga), the cause (Hetu), the one bound with a rope at the waist (Damodara), the patient (Saha), the bearer of the earth (Mahidhara), the most fortunate (Mahabhaga), the swift (Vegavan) and the one who consumes without limit (Amitashana).

items.text:
उद्भवः क्षोभणो देवः श्रीगर्भः परमेश्वरः।
करणं कारणं कर्ता विकर्ता गहनो गुहः॥४१॥
items.tr:
udbhavaḥ kṣobhaṇo devaḥ śrīgarbhaḥ parameśvaraḥ|
karaṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ kartā vikartā gahano guhaḥ||41||
items.en: He is the origin (Udbhava), the one who stirs things up (Kshobhana), the shining God (Deva), the one who holds Lakshmi within (Shrigarbha), the Supreme Lord (Parameshvara), the instrument (Karana), the cause (Karana), the doer (Karta), the one who makes variety (Vikarta), the deep (Gahana) and the hidden (Guha).

items.text:
व्यवसायो व्यवस्थानः संस्थानः स्थानदो ध्रुवः।
परर्द्धिः परमस्पष्टस्तुष्टः पुष्टः शुभेक्षणः॥४२॥
items.tr:
vyavasāyo vyavasthānaḥ saṃsthānaḥ sthānado dhruvaḥ|
pararddhiḥ paramaspaṣṭastuṣṭaḥ puṣṭaḥ śubhekṣaṇaḥ||42||
items.en: He is resolve (Vyavasaya), the one who sets all in order (Vyavasthana), the final resting place (Samsthana), giver of position (Sthanada), the fixed (Dhruva), of supreme wealth (Pararddhi), the clearest (Paramaspashta), content (Tushta), full (Pushta) and of auspicious gaze (Shubhekshana).

items.text:
रामो विरामो विरजो (or विरतो) मार्गो नेयो नयोऽनयः।
वीरः शक्तिमतां श्रेष्ठो धर्मो धर्मविदुत्तमः॥४३॥
items.tr:
rāmo virāmo virajo (or virato) mārgo neyo nayo'nayaḥ|
vīraḥ śaktimatāṃ śreṣṭho dharmo dharmaviduttamaḥ||43||
items.en: He is the delight (Rama), the place of rest (Virama), the stainless (Viraja), the path (Marga), the one to be led to (Neya), the guide (Naya), the one no one leads (Anaya), the hero (Vira), the best of the strong (Shaktimatam Shreshtha), dharma itself (Dharma) and the greatest knower of dharma (Dharmaviduttama).

items.text:
वैकुण्ठः पुरुषः प्राणः प्राणदः प्रणवः पृथुः।
हिरण्यगर्भः शत्रुघ्नो व्याप्तो वायुरधोक्षजः॥४४॥
items.tr:
vaikuṇṭhaḥ puruṣaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇadaḥ praṇavaḥ pṛthuḥ|
hiraṇyagarbhaḥ śatrughno vyāpto vāyuradhokṣajaḥ||44||
items.en: He is the lord of Vaikuntha (Vaikuntha), the Person (Purusha), breath (Prana), giver of breath (Pranada), the sacred syllable Om (Pranava), the vast (Prithu), the golden womb (Hiranyagarbha), slayer of enemies (Shatrughna), the all-pervading (Vyapta), the wind (Vayu) and the one beyond sense knowledge (Adhokshaja).

items.text:
ऋतुः सुदर्शनः कालः परमेष्ठी परिग्रहः।
उग्रः संवत्सरो दक्षो विश्रामो विश्वदक्षिणः॥४५॥
items.tr:
ṛtuḥ sudarśanaḥ kālaḥ parameṣṭhī parigrahaḥ|
ugraḥ saṃvatsaro dakṣo viśrāmo viśvadakṣiṇaḥ||45||
items.en: He is the season (Ritu), the one of pleasing sight (Sudarshana), time (Kala), the one in the highest place (Parameshthi), the one who accepts (Parigraha), the fierce (Ugra), the year (Samvatsara), the skilful (Daksha), the place of rest (Vishrama) and the most generous to all (Vishvadakshina).

items.text:
विस्तारः स्थावरस्थाणुः प्रमाणं बीजमव्ययम्।
अर्थोऽनर्थो महाकोशो महाभोगो महाधनः॥४६॥
items.tr:
vistāraḥ sthāvarasthāṇuḥ pramāṇaṃ bījamavyayam|
artho'nartho mahākośo mahābhogo mahādhanaḥ||46||
items.en: He is the expanse (Vistara), the firm support of the unmoving (Sthavarasthanu), the measure of truth (Pramana), the undying seed (Bijam Avyayam), the aim (Artha), the one who needs nothing (Anartha), the great treasure-house (Mahakosha), the great enjoyment (Mahabhoga) and of great wealth (Mahadhana).

items.text:
अनिर्विण्णः स्थविष्ठोऽभूर्धर्मयूपो महामखः।
नक्षत्रनेमिर्नक्षत्री क्षमः क्षामः समीहनः॥४७॥
items.tr:
anirviṇṇaḥ sthaviṣṭho'bhūrdharmayūpo mahāmakhaḥ|
nakṣatranemirnakṣatrī kṣamaḥ kṣāmaḥ samīhanaḥ||47||
items.en: He is never weary (Anirvinna), the most massive (Sthavishtha), unborn (Abhu), the post of dharma (Dharmayupa), the great sacrifice (Mahamakha), the hub of the stars (Nakshatranemi), lord of the stars (Nakshatri), the able (Kshama), the one who remains when all wastes away (Kshama) and the one who wills (Samihana).

items.text:
यज्ञ इज्यो महेज्यश्च क्रतुः सत्रं सतां गतिः।
सर्वदर्शी विमुक्तात्मा सर्वज्ञो ज्ञानमुत्तमम्॥४८॥
items.tr:
yajña ijyo mahejyaśca kratuḥ satraṃ satāṃ gatiḥ|
sarvadarśī vimuktātmā sarvajño jñānamuttamam||48||
items.en: He is the sacrifice (Yajna), the one to be worshipped (Ijya), most worthy of worship (Mahejya), the rite (Kratu), the long sacrifice (Satra), the goal of the good (Satam Gati), the all-seeing (Sarvadarshi), of free nature (Vimuktatma), all-knowing (Sarvajna) and the highest knowledge (Jnanam Uttamam).

items.text:
सुव्रतः सुमुखः सूक्ष्मः सुघोषः सुखदः सुहृत्।
मनोहरो जितक्रोधो वीरबाहुर्विदारणः॥४९॥
items.tr:
suvrataḥ sumukhaḥ sūkṣmaḥ sughoṣaḥ sukhadaḥ suhṛt|
manoharo jitakrodho vīrabāhurvidāraṇaḥ||49||
items.en: He keeps good vows (Suvrata), has a lovely face (Sumukha), is subtle (Sukshma), of pleasing sound (Sughosha), giver of happiness (Sukhada), the good friend (Suhrit), charming the mind (Manohara), the conqueror of anger (Jitakrodha), of heroic arms (Virabahu) and the one who tears apart the wicked (Vidarana).

items.text:
स्वापनः स्ववशो व्यापी नैकात्मा नैककर्मकृत्।
वत्सरो वत्सलो वत्सी रत्नगर्भो धनेश्वरः॥५०॥
items.tr:
svāpanaḥ svavaśo vyāpī naikātmā naikakarmakṛt|
vatsaro vatsalo vatsī ratnagarbho dhaneśvaraḥ||50||
items.en: He puts beings to sleep (Svapana), depends on none (Svavasha), pervades all (Vyapi), has many selves (Naikatma), does many deeds (Naikakarmakrit), is the year (Vatsara), loving like a parent (Vatsala), the one who cares for his children (Vatsi), holds jewels within (Ratnagarbha) and is lord of wealth (Dhaneshvara).

items.text:
धर्मगुब्धर्मकृद्धर्मी सदसत्क्षरमक्षरम्।
अविज्ञाता सहस्रांशुर्विधाता कृतलक्षणः॥५१॥
items.tr:
dharmagubdharmakṛddharmī sadasatkṣaramakṣaram|
avijñātā sahasrāṃśurvidhātā kṛtalakṣaṇaḥ||51||
items.en: He protects dharma (Dharmagup), practises dharma (Dharmakrit), upholds dharma (Dharmi); he is what is and what is not (Sadasat), the perishable and the imperishable (Ksharam Aksharam), the one who does not know as others know (Avijnata), thousand-rayed (Sahasramshu), the arranger (Vidhata) and the one of well-known marks (Kritalakshana).

items.text:
गभस्तिनेमिः सत्त्वस्थः सिंहो भूतमहेश्वरः।
आदिदेवो महादेवो देवेशो देवभृद्गुरुः॥५२॥
items.tr:
gabhastinemiḥ sattvasthaḥ siṃho bhūtamaheśvaraḥ|
ādidevo mahādevo deveśo devabhṛdguruḥ||52||
items.en: He is the hub of the rays (Gabhastinemi), dwells in goodness (Sattvastha), is the lion (Simha), the great lord of beings (Bhutamaheshvara), the first God (Adideva), the great God (Mahadeva), lord of the gods (Devesha) and their supporter and teacher (Devabhrid Guru).

items.text:
उत्तरो गोपतिर्गोप्ता ज्ञानगम्यः पुरातनः।
शरीरभूतभृद्भोक्ता कपीन्द्रो भूरिदक्षिणः॥५३॥
items.tr:
uttaro gopatirgoptā jñānagamyaḥ purātanaḥ|
śarīrabhūtabhṛdbhoktā kapīndro bhūridakṣiṇaḥ||53||
items.en: He is the one who lifts beings across (Uttara), lord of cows (Gopati), the protector (Gopta), reached by knowledge (Jnanagamya), the ancient (Puratana), supporter of the elements of the body (Sharirabhutabhrit), the enjoyer (Bhokta), lord of the monkeys (Kapindra) and the one who gives great gifts (Bhuridakshina).

items.text:
सोमपोऽमृतपः सोमः पुरुजित्पुरुसत्तमः।
विनयो जयः सत्यसंधो दाशार्हः सात्त्वतांपतिः॥५४॥
items.tr:
somapo'mṛtapaḥ somaḥ purujitpurusattamaḥ|
vinayo jayaḥ satyasaṃdho dāśārhaḥ sāttvatāṃpatiḥ||54||
items.en: He drinks the Soma (Somapa), drinks nectar (Amritapa), is the moon (Soma), conquers many (Purujit), is the best among many (Purusattama), the one who disciplines (Vinaya), victory (Jaya), true to his promise (Satyasandha), the descendant of Dasharha (Dasharha) and lord of the Satvatas (Satvatam Pati).

items.text:
जीवो विनयिता साक्षी मुकुन्दोऽमितविक्रमः।
अम्भोनिधिरनन्तात्मा महोदधिशयोऽन्तकः॥५५॥
items.tr:
jīvo vinayitā sākṣī mukundo'mitavikramaḥ|
ambhonidhiranantātmā mahodadhiśayo'ntakaḥ||55||
items.en: He is the living soul (Jiva), the guide to good conduct (Vinayita), the witness (Sakshi), the giver of freedom (Mukunda), of boundless valour (Amitavikrama), the ocean (Ambhonidhi), of endless nature (Anantatma), the one who lies on the great ocean (Mahodadhishaya) and the one who ends all (Antaka).

items.text:
अजो महार्हः स्वाभाव्यो जितामित्रः प्रमोदनः।
आनन्दो नन्दनो नन्दः सत्यधर्मा त्रिविक्रमः॥५६॥
items.tr:
ajo mahārhaḥ svābhāvyo jitāmitraḥ pramodanaḥ|
ānando nandano nandaḥ satyadharmā trivikramaḥ||56||
items.en: He is unborn (Aja), most worthy of honour (Maharha), true to his own nature (Svabhavya), conqueror of foes (Jitamitra), the giver of delight (Pramodana), bliss (Ananda), the one who delights others (Nandana), joy (Nanda), the one whose dharma is true (Satyadharma) and the one who took three great strides (Trivikrama).

items.text:
महर्षिः कपिलाचार्यः कृतज्ञो मेदिनीपतिः।
त्रिपदस्त्रिदशाध्यक्षो महाशृङ्गः कृतान्तकृत्॥५७॥
items.tr:
maharṣiḥ kapilācāryaḥ kṛtajño medinīpatiḥ|
tripadastridaśādhyakṣo mahāśṛṅgaḥ kṛtāntakṛt||57||
items.en: He is the great sage (Maharshi), the teacher Kapila (Kapilacharya), the one who knows what was done (Kritajna), lord of the earth (Medinipati), the one of three steps (Tripada), overseer of the gods (Tridashadhyaksha), the great-horned fish (Mahashringa) and the one who ends death itself (Kritantakrit).

items.text:
महावराहो गोविन्दः सुषेणः कनकाङ्गदी।
गुह्यो गभीरो गहनो गुप्तश्चक्रगदाधरः॥५८॥
items.tr:
mahāvarāho govindaḥ suṣeṇaḥ kanakāṅgadī|
guhyo gabhīro gahano guptaścakragadādharaḥ||58||
items.en: He is the great boar (Mahavaraha), the finder of the earth (Govinda), the one with a fine army (Sushena), wearer of golden armlets (Kanakangadi), the secret (Guhya), the deep (Gabhira), the hard to enter (Gahana), the hidden (Gupta) and the bearer of discus and mace (Chakragadadhara).

items.text:
वेधाः स्वाङ्गोऽजितः कृष्णो दृढः संकर्षणोऽच्युतः।
वरुणो वारुणो वृक्षः पुष्कराक्षो महामनाः॥५९॥
items.tr:
vedhāḥ svāṅgo'jitaḥ kṛṣṇo dṛḍhaḥ saṃkarṣaṇo'cyutaḥ|
varuṇo vāruṇo vṛkṣaḥ puṣkarākṣo mahāmanāḥ||59||
items.en: He is the creator (Vedha), his own instrument (Svanga), the unconquered (Ajita), Krishna, the firm (Dridha), the one who draws all in (Sankarshana), the one who never falls (Achyuta), Varuna, the son of Varuna (Varuna), the tree (Vriksha), lotus-eyed (Pushkaraksha) and great-minded (Mahamana).

items.text:
भगवान् भगहाऽऽनन्दी वनमाली हलायुधः।
आदित्यो ज्योतिरादित्यः सहिष्णुर्गतिसत्तमः॥६०॥
items.tr:
bhagavān bhagahā''nandī vanamālī halāyudhaḥ|
ādityo jyotirādityaḥ sahiṣṇurgatisattamaḥ||60||
items.en: He is the Blessed Lord (Bhagavan), the one who takes away power at the end (Bhagaha), the joyful (Anandi), wearer of the forest garland (Vanamali), the one armed with the plough (Halayudha), the son of Aditi (Aditya), the sun of light (Jyotiraditya), the patient (Sahishnu) and the best goal (Gatisattama).

items.text:
सुधन्वा खण्डपरशुर्दारुणो द्रविणप्रदः।
दिवःस्पृक् सर्वदृग्व्यासो वाचस्पतिरयोनिजः॥६१॥
items.tr:
sudhanvā khaṇḍaparaśurdāruṇo draviṇapradaḥ|
divaḥspṛk sarvadṛgvyāso vācaspatirayonijaḥ||61||
items.en: He has a fine bow (Sudhanva), the axe that cuts down foes (Khandaparashu), is fierce to the wicked (Daruna), the giver of wealth (Dravinaprada), the one who touches heaven (Divahsprik), the all-seeing (Sarvadrik), the arranger of the Vedas (Vyasa), lord of speech (Vachaspati) and not born of a womb (Ayonija).

items.text:
त्रिसामा सामगः साम निर्वाणं भेषजं भिषक्।
संन्यासकृच्छमः शान्तो निष्ठा शान्तिः परायणम्॥६२॥
items.tr:
trisāmā sāmagaḥ sāma nirvāṇaṃ bheṣajaṃ bhiṣak|
saṃnyāsakṛcchamaḥ śānto niṣṭhā śāntiḥ parāyaṇam||62||
items.en: He is praised by the three Samans (Trisama), the singer of the Sama (Samaga), the Sama chant itself (Sama), final freedom (Nirvana), the medicine (Bheshaja), the physician (Bhishak), the one who set up the life of renunciation (Sannyasakrit), calm (Shama), peaceful (Shanta), the final ground (Nishtha), peace (Shanti) and the highest refuge (Parayana).

items.text:
शुभाङ्गः शान्तिदः स्रष्टा कुमुदः कुवलेशयः।
गोहितो गोपतिर्गोप्ता वृषभाक्षो वृषप्रियः॥६३॥
items.tr:
śubhāṅgaḥ śāntidaḥ sraṣṭā kumudaḥ kuvaleśayaḥ|
gohito gopatirgoptā vṛṣabhākṣo vṛṣapriyaḥ||63||
items.en: He has beautiful limbs (Shubhanga), gives peace (Shantida), is the creator (Srashta), the joy of the earth (Kumuda), the one who lies in the waters (Kuvaleshaya), the friend of cows (Gohita), lord of cows (Gopati), the protector (Gopta), the one whose eye is dharma (Vrishabhaksha) and the lover of dharma (Vrishapriya).

items.text:
अनिवर्ती निवृत्तात्मा संक्षेप्ता क्षेमकृच्छिवः।
श्रीवत्सवक्षाः श्रीवासः श्रीपतिः श्रीमतांवरः॥६४॥
items.tr:
anivartī nivṛttātmā saṃkṣeptā kṣemakṛcchivaḥ|
śrīvatsavakṣāḥ śrīvāsaḥ śrīpatiḥ śrīmatāṃvaraḥ||64||
items.en: He never turns back (Anivarti), is of detached nature (Nivrittatma), the one who draws all back in (Sankshepta), maker of welfare (Kshemakrit), the auspicious (Shiva), bearer of the Shrivatsa on his chest (Shrivatsavaksha), the dwelling of Lakshmi (Shrivasa), her husband (Shripati) and the best of the glorious (Shrimatam Vara).

items.text:
श्रीदः श्रीशः श्रीनिवासः श्रीनिधिः श्रीविभावनः।
श्रीधरः श्रीकरः श्रेयः श्रीमाँल्लोकत्रयाश्रयः॥६५॥
items.tr:
śrīdaḥ śrīśaḥ śrīnivāsaḥ śrīnidhiḥ śrīvibhāvanaḥ|
śrīdharaḥ śrīkaraḥ śreyaḥ śrīmām̐llokatrayāśrayaḥ||65||
items.en: He gives fortune (Shrida), is lord of fortune (Shrisha), the dwelling of fortune (Shrinivasa), the treasury of fortune (Shrinidhi), the one who spreads fortune (Shrivibhavana), the holder of Lakshmi (Shridhara), the maker of fortune (Shrikara), the highest good (Shreya), the glorious (Shriman) and the refuge of the three worlds (Lokatrayashraya).

items.text:
स्वक्षः स्वङ्गः शतानन्दो नन्दिर्ज्योतिर्गणेश्वरः।
विजितात्माऽविधेयात्मा सत्कीर्तिश्छिन्नसंशयः॥६६॥
items.tr:
svakṣaḥ svaṅgaḥ śatānando nandirjyotirgaṇeśvaraḥ|
vijitātmā'vidheyātmā satkīrtiśchinnasaṃśayaḥ||66||
items.en: He has lovely eyes (Svaksha), lovely limbs (Svanga), a hundred joys (Shatananda), is joy (Nandi), lord of the hosts of light (Jyotirganeshvara), self-controlled (Vijitatma), ruled by no one (Avidheyatma), of true fame (Satkirti) and the remover of doubts (Chhinnasamshaya).

items.text:
उदीर्णः सर्वतश्चक्षुरनीशः शाश्वतस्थिरः।
भूशयो भूषणो भूतिर्विशोकः शोकनाशनः॥६७॥
items.tr:
udīrṇaḥ sarvataścakṣuranīśaḥ śāśvatasthiraḥ|
bhūśayo bhūṣaṇo bhūtirviśokaḥ śokanāśanaḥ||67||
items.en: He is exalted (Udirna), has eyes on all sides (Sarvatashchakshu), has no lord above him (Anisha), is eternal and steady (Shashvatasthira), the one who lay on the ground (Bhushaya), the adornment of the earth (Bhushana), prosperity (Bhuti), free of sorrow (Vishoka) and the destroyer of sorrow (Shokanashana).

items.text:
अर्चिष्मानर्चितः कुम्भो विशुद्धात्मा विशोधनः।
अनिरुद्धोऽप्रतिरथः प्रद्युम्नोऽमितविक्रमः॥६८॥
items.tr:
arciṣmānarcitaḥ kumbho viśuddhātmā viśodhanaḥ|
aniruddho'pratirathaḥ pradyumno'mitavikramaḥ||68||
items.en: He is radiant (Archishman), the one worshipped (Archita), the vessel that holds all (Kumbha), of pure nature (Vishuddhatma), the purifier (Vishodhana), the unstoppable (Aniruddha), the one without a rival (Apratiratha), the one of great wealth (Pradyumna) and of boundless valour (Amitavikrama).

items.text:
कालनेमिनिहा वीरः शौरिः शूरजनेश्वरः।
त्रिलोकात्मा त्रिलोकेशः केशवः केशिहा हरिः॥६९॥
items.tr:
kālaneminihā vīraḥ śauriḥ śūrajaneśvaraḥ|
trilokātmā trilokeśaḥ keśavaḥ keśihā hariḥ||69||
items.en: He is the slayer of the demon Kalanemi (Kalaneminiha), the hero (Vira), the descendant of Shura (Shauri), lord of the brave (Shurajaneshvara), the self of the three worlds (Trilokatma), lord of the three worlds (Trilokesha), the long-haired one (Keshava), slayer of the demon Keshi (Keshiha) and the remover of sin (Hari).

items.text:
कामदेवः कामपालः कामी कान्तः कृतागमः।
अनिर्देश्यवपुर्विष्णुर्वीरोऽनन्तो धनंजयः॥७०॥
items.tr:
kāmadevaḥ kāmapālaḥ kāmī kāntaḥ kṛtāgamaḥ|
anirdeśyavapurviṣṇurvīro'nanto dhanaṃjayaḥ||70||
items.en: He is the god of love (Kamadeva), the guardian of desires (Kamapala), the one who has all desires fulfilled (Kami), the lovely (Kanta), the giver of scriptures (Kritagama), of indescribable form (Anirdeshyavapu), the all-pervading (Vishnu), the hero (Vira), the endless (Ananta) and the winner of wealth (Dhananjaya).

items.text:
ब्रह्मण्यो ब्रह्मकृद् ब्रह्मा ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविवर्धनः।
ब्रह्मविद् ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मी ब्रह्मज्ञो ब्राह्मणप्रियः॥७१॥
items.tr:
brahmaṇyo brahmakṛd brahmā brahma brahmavivardhanaḥ|
brahmavid brāhmaṇo brahmī brahmajño brāhmaṇapriyaḥ||71||
items.en: He is devoted to Brahman (Brahmanya), the maker of the Vedas and of austerity (Brahmakrit), the creator Brahma, Brahman itself, the one who makes the Vedas grow (Brahmavivardhana), the knower of Brahman (Brahmavid), the Brahmin (Brahmana), the one who has Brahman (Brahmi), the knower of the Vedas (Brahmajna) and dear to Brahmins (Brahmanapriya).

items.text:
महाक्रमो महाकर्मा महातेजा महोरगः।
महाक्रतुर्महायज्वा महायज्ञो महाहविः॥७२॥
items.tr:
mahākramo mahākarmā mahātejā mahoragaḥ|
mahākraturmahāyajvā mahāyajño mahāhaviḥ||72||
items.en: He takes great steps (Mahakrama), does great deeds (Mahakarma), has great brilliance (Mahateja), is the great serpent (Mahoraga), the great rite (Mahakratu), the great sacrificer (Mahayajva), the great sacrifice (Mahayajna) and the great offering (Mahahavi).

items.text:
स्तव्यः स्तवप्रियः स्तोत्रं स्तुतिः स्तोता रणप्रियः।
पूर्णः पूरयिता पुण्यः पुण्यकीर्तिरनामयः॥७३॥
items.tr:
stavyaḥ stavapriyaḥ stotraṃ stutiḥ stotā raṇapriyaḥ|
pūrṇaḥ pūrayitā puṇyaḥ puṇyakīrtiranāmayaḥ||73||
items.en: He is worthy of praise (Stavya), fond of praise (Stavapriya), the hymn (Stotra), the act of praise (Stuti), the one who praises (Stota), fond of battle (Ranapriya), full (Purna), the one who fills (Purayita), holy (Punya), of holy fame (Punyakirti) and free of disease (Anamaya).

items.text:
मनोजवस्तीर्थकरो वसुरेता वसुप्रदः।
वसुप्रदो वासुदेवो वसुर्वसुमना हविः॥७४॥
items.tr:
manojavastīrthakaro vasuretā vasupradaḥ|
vasuprado vāsudevo vasurvasumanā haviḥ||74||
items.en: He is swift as the mind (Manojava), the maker of holy places and teachings (Tirthakara), whose seed is golden (Vasureta), the giver of wealth (Vasuprada), again the giver of wealth (Vasuprada), the son of Vasudeva (Vasudeva), the dweller in all (Vasu), of generous mind (Vasumana) and the offering (Havi).

items.text:
सद्गतिः सत्कृतिः सत्ता सद्भूतिः सत्परायणः।
शूरसेनो यदुश्रेष्ठः सन्निवासः सुयामुनः॥७५॥
items.tr:
sadgatiḥ satkṛtiḥ sattā sadbhūtiḥ satparāyaṇaḥ|
śūraseno yaduśreṣṭhaḥ sannivāsaḥ suyāmunaḥ||75||
items.en: He is the goal of the good (Sadgati), good action (Satkriti), being itself (Satta), true glory (Sadbhuti), the highest goal of the good (Satparayana), the one whose army is brave (Shurasena), the best of the Yadus (Yadushreshtha), the dwelling of the good (Sannivasa) and the one of the Yamuna banks (Suyamuna).

items.text:
भूतावासो वासुदेवः सर्वासुनिलयोऽनलः।
दर्पहा दर्पदो दृप्तो दुर्धरोऽथापराजितः॥७६॥
items.tr:
bhūtāvāso vāsudevaḥ sarvāsunilayo'nalaḥ|
darpahā darpado dṛpto durdharo'thāparājitaḥ||76||
items.en: He is the dwelling of beings (Bhutavasa), the god who dwells in all (Vasudeva), the resting place of all lives (Sarvasunilaya), fire that is never enough (Anala), destroyer of pride (Darpaha), giver of pride in dharma (Darpada), the joyful (Dripta), hard to hold (Durdhara) and the unconquered (Aparajita).

items.text:
विश्वमूर्तिर्महामूर्तिर्दीप्तमूर्तिरमूर्तिमान्।
अनेकमूर्तिरव्यक्तः शतमूर्तिः शताननः॥७७॥
items.tr:
viśvamūrtirmahāmūrtirdīptamūrtiramūrtimān|
anekamūrtiravyaktaḥ śatamūrtiḥ śatānanaḥ||77||
items.en: He is the universe as his form (Vishvamurti), of great form (Mahamurti), of blazing form (Diptamurti), without form (Amurtiman), of many forms (Anekamurti), unmanifest (Avyakta), of a hundred forms (Shatamurti) and of a hundred faces (Shatanana).

items.text:
एको नैकः सवः कः किं यत् तत्पदमनुत्तमम्।
लोकबन्धुर्लोकनाथो माधवो भक्तवत्सलः॥७८॥
items.tr:
eko naikaḥ savaḥ kaḥ kiṃ yat tatpadamanuttamam|
lokabandhurlokanātho mādhavo bhaktavatsalaḥ||78||
items.en: He is the One (Eka), the many (Naika), the Soma rite (Sava), bliss (Ka), the one asked about (Kim), the one from whom all comes (Yat), That (Tat), the highest state (Padam Anuttamam), the kinsman of the world (Lokabandhu), lord of the world (Lokanatha), lord of Lakshmi (Madhava) and the one who loves his devotees (Bhaktavatsala).

items.text:
सुवर्णवर्णो हेमाङ्गो वराङ्गश्चन्दनाङ्गदी।
वीरहा विषमः शून्यो घृताशीरचलश्चलः॥७९॥
items.tr:
suvarṇavarṇo hemāṅgo varāṅgaścandanāṅgadī|
vīrahā viṣamaḥ śūnyo ghṛtāśīracalaścalaḥ||79||
items.en: He is golden in colour (Suvarnavarna), with a golden body (Hemanga), of fine limbs (Varanga), wearing sandal paste and armlets (Chandanangadi), slayer of demon heroes (Viraha), the unequalled (Vishama), the void (Shunya), the one who needs no blessings (Ghritashi), the unmoving (Achala) and the moving (Chala).

items.text:
अमानी मानदो मान्यो लोकस्वामी त्रिलोकधृक्।
सुमेधा मेधजो धन्यः सत्यमेधा धराधरः॥८०॥
items.tr:
amānī mānado mānyo lokasvāmī trilokadhṛk|
sumedhā medhajo dhanyaḥ satyamedhā dharādharaḥ||80||
items.en: He is free of pride (Amani), the giver of honour (Manada), the one to be honoured (Manya), master of the world (Lokasvami), bearer of the three worlds (Trilokadhrik), of fine intelligence (Sumedha), born of the sacrifice (Medhaja), blessed (Dhanya), of true intelligence (Satyamedha) and bearer of the earth (Dharadhara).

items.text:
तेजोवृषो द्युतिधरः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः।
प्रग्रहो निग्रहो व्यग्रो नैकशृङ्गो गदाग्रजः॥८१॥
items.tr:
tejovṛṣo dyutidharaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ|
pragraho nigraho vyagro naikaśṛṅgo gadāgrajaḥ||81||
items.en: He showers brilliance (Tejovrisha), holds splendour (Dyutidhara), is the best of all who bear weapons (Sarvashastrabhritam Vara), the one who accepts offerings (Pragraha), the one who restrains (Nigraha), the one never at a loss (Vyagra), the many-horned one (Naikashringa) and the elder brother of Gada (Gadagraja).

items.text:
चतुर्मूर्तिश्चतुर्बाहुश्चतुर्व्यूहश्चतुर्गतिः।
चतुरात्मा चतुर्भावश्चतुर्वेदविदेकपात्॥८२॥
items.tr:
caturmūrtiścaturbāhuścaturvyūhaścaturgatiḥ|
caturātmā caturbhāvaścaturvedavidekapāt||82||
items.en: He has four forms (Chaturmurti), four arms (Chaturbahu), four manifestations (Chaturvyuha), is the goal of the four orders of life (Chaturgati), fourfold in self (Chaturatma), the source of the four aims of life (Chaturbhava), the knower of the four Vedas (Chaturvedavid) and the one of whom a single part is the world (Ekapat).

items.text:
समावर्तोऽनिवृत्तात्मा दुर्जयो दुरतिक्रमः।
दुर्लभो दुर्गमो दुर्गो दुरावासो दुरारिहा॥८३॥
items.tr:
samāvarto'nivṛttātmā durjayo duratikramaḥ|
durlabho durgamo durgo durāvāso durārihā||83||
items.en: He turns the wheel of life (Samavarta), never turns away (Anivrittatma), is hard to conquer (Durjaya), hard to go beyond (Duratikrama), hard to reach (Durlabha), hard to approach (Durgama), hard to attain (Durga), hard to make his dwelling (Duravasa) and the slayer of evil foes (Durariha).

items.text:
शुभाङ्गो लोकसारङ्गः सुतन्तुस्तन्तुवर्धनः।
इन्द्रकर्मा महाकर्मा कृतकर्मा कृतागमः॥८४॥
items.tr:
śubhāṅgo lokasāraṅgaḥ sutantustantuvardhanaḥ|
indrakarmā mahākarmā kṛtakarmā kṛtāgamaḥ||84||
items.en: He has fair limbs (Shubhanga), takes the essence of the world (Lokasaranga), is the fine thread (Sutantu), the one who extends the thread of the world (Tantuvardhana), whose deeds are like Indra's (Indrakarma), of great deeds (Mahakarma), whose work is done (Kritakarma) and the author of the scriptures (Kritagama).

items.text:
उद्भवः सुन्दरः सुन्दो रत्ननाभः सुलोचनः।
अर्को वाजसनः शृङ्गी जयन्तः सर्वविज्जयी॥८५॥
items.tr:
udbhavaḥ sundaraḥ sundo ratnanābhaḥ sulocanaḥ|
arko vājasanaḥ śṛṅgī jayantaḥ sarvavijjayī||85||
items.en: He is the source (Udbhava), the beautiful (Sundara), the compassionate (Sunda), jewel-navelled (Ratnanabha), of lovely eyes (Sulochana), the sun (Arka), the giver of food (Vajasana), the horned one (Shringi), the victor (Jayanta), the all-knowing (Sarvavit) and the one who always wins (Jayi).

items.text:
सुवर्णबिन्दुरक्षोभ्यः सर्ववागीश्वरेश्वरः।
महाह्रदो महागर्तो महाभूतो महानिधिः॥८६॥
items.tr:
suvarṇabindurakṣobhyaḥ sarvavāgīśvareśvaraḥ|
mahāhrado mahāgarto mahābhūto mahānidhiḥ||86||
items.en: He has golden limbs (Suvarnabindu), is unshakeable (Akshobhya), the lord of all lords of speech (Sarvavagishvareshvara), the great lake (Mahahrada), the great abyss (Mahagarta), the great Being (Mahabhuta) and the great treasure (Mahanidhi).

items.text:
कुमुदः कुन्दरः कुन्दः पर्जन्यः पावनोऽनिलः।
अमृतांशोऽमृतवपुः सर्वज्ञः सर्वतोमुखः॥८७॥
items.tr:
kumudaḥ kundaraḥ kundaḥ parjanyaḥ pāvano'nilaḥ|
amṛtāṃśo'mṛtavapuḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvatomukhaḥ||87||
items.en: He is the joy of the earth (Kumuda), the giver of the earth (Kundara), as pure as jasmine (Kunda), the rain cloud (Parjanya), the purifier (Pavana), the wind (Anila), the source of nectar (Amritamsha), of immortal body (Amritavapu), all-knowing (Sarvajna) and with faces on every side (Sarvatomukha).

items.text:
सुलभः सुव्रतः सिद्धः शत्रुजिच्छत्रुतापनः।
न्यग्रोधोऽदुम्बरोऽश्वत्थश्चाणूरान्ध्रनिषूदनः॥८८॥
items.tr:
sulabhaḥ suvrataḥ siddhaḥ śatrujicchatrutāpanaḥ|
nyagrodho'dumbaro'śvatthaścāṇūrāndhraniṣūdanaḥ||88||
items.en: He is easy to reach (Sulabha), keeps fine vows (Suvrata), is perfect (Siddha), conquers enemies (Shatrujit), burns enemies (Shatrutapana), is the banyan, the fig and the holy fig tree (Nyagrodha, Udumbara, Ashvattha) and the slayer of Chanura of Andhra (Chanurandhranishudana).

items.text:
सहस्रार्चिः सप्तजिह्वः सप्तैधाः सप्तवाहनः।
अमूर्तिरनघोऽचिन्त्यो भयकृद्भयनाशनः॥८९॥
items.tr:
sahasrārciḥ saptajihvaḥ saptaidhāḥ saptavāhanaḥ|
amūrtiranagho'cintyo bhayakṛdbhayanāśanaḥ||89||
items.en: He has a thousand flames (Sahasrarchi), seven tongues (Saptajihva), seven fires (Saptaidha), seven horses (Saptavahana); he is formless (Amurti), sinless (Anagha), beyond thought (Achintya), the one who causes fear to the wicked (Bhayakrit) and the destroyer of fear (Bhayanashana).

items.text:
अणुर्बृहत्कृशः स्थूलो गुणभृन्निर्गुणो महान्।
अधृतः स्वधृतः स्वास्यः प्राग्वंशो वंशवर्धनः॥९०॥
items.tr:
aṇurbṛhatkṛśaḥ sthūlo guṇabhṛnnirguṇo mahān|
adhṛtaḥ svadhṛtaḥ svāsyaḥ prāgvaṃśo vaṃśavardhanaḥ||90||
items.en: He is tiny (Anu), vast (Brihat), thin (Krisha), large (Sthula), the bearer of qualities (Gunabhrit), free of qualities (Nirguna), great (Mahan), held up by nothing (Adhrita), self-supported (Svadhrita), of fine face (Svasya), of the first family (Pragvamsha) and the one who makes families grow (Vamshavardhana).

items.text:
भारभृत् कथितो योगी योगीशः सर्वकामदः।
आश्रमः श्रमणः क्षामः सुपर्णो वायुवाहनः॥९१॥
items.tr:
bhārabhṛt kathito yogī yogīśaḥ sarvakāmadaḥ|
āśramaḥ śramaṇaḥ kṣāmaḥ suparṇo vāyuvāhanaḥ||91||
items.en: He bears the burden of the world (Bharabhrit), is the one spoken of in scripture (Kathita), the yogi (Yogi), lord of yogis (Yogisha), giver of all desires (Sarvakamada), the place of rest (Ashrama), the one who troubles the worldly (Shramana), the one who wastes away all at the end (Kshama), the fair-winged bird (Suparna) and the mover of the winds (Vayuvahana).

items.text:
धनुर्धरो धनुर्वेदो दण्डो दमयिता दमः।
अपराजितः सर्वसहो नियन्ताऽनियमोऽयमः॥९२॥
items.tr:
dhanurdharo dhanurvedo daṇḍo damayitā damaḥ|
aparājitaḥ sarvasaho niyantā'niyamo'yamaḥ||92||
items.en: He bears the bow (Dhanurdhara), is the science of archery (Dhanurveda), the rod of law (Danda), the one who tames (Damayita), self-restraint (Dama), the unconquered (Aparajita), the one who bears all (Sarvasaha), the controller (Niyanta), free of rules (Aniyama) and free of death's control (Ayama).

items.text:
सत्त्ववान् सात्त्विकः सत्यः सत्यधर्मपरायणः।
अभिप्रायः प्रियार्होऽर्हः प्रियकृत् प्रीतिवर्धनः॥९३॥
items.tr:
sattvavān sāttvikaḥ satyaḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ|
abhiprāyaḥ priyārho'rhaḥ priyakṛt prītivardhanaḥ||93||
items.en: He is full of goodness (Sattvavan), pure in nature (Sattvika), the truth (Satya), devoted to truth and dharma (Satyadharmaparayana), the one sought by all (Abhipraya), worthy of love (Priyarha), worthy (Arha), the one who does what pleases (Priyakrit) and the one who increases joy (Pritivardhana).

items.text:
विहायसगतिर्ज्योतिः सुरुचिर्हुतभुग्विभुः।
रविर्विरोचनः सूर्यः सविता रविलोचनः॥९४॥
items.tr:
vihāyasagatirjyotiḥ surucirhutabhugvibhuḥ|
ravirvirocanaḥ sūryaḥ savitā ravilocanaḥ||94||
items.en: He moves through the sky (Vihayasagati), is light (Jyoti), of lovely radiance (Suruchi), the fire that eats the offerings (Hutabhuk), the all-pervading (Vibhu), the sun (Ravi), the shining one (Virochana), the sun (Surya), the begetter (Savita) and the one whose eye is the sun (Ravilochana).

items.text:
अनन्तो हुतभुग्भोक्ता सुखदो नैकजोऽग्रजः।
अनिर्विण्णः सदामर्षी लोकाधिष्ठानमद्भुतः॥९५॥
items.tr:
ananto hutabhugbhoktā sukhado naikajo'grajaḥ|
anirviṇṇaḥ sadāmarṣī lokādhiṣṭhānamadbhutaḥ||95||
items.en: He is endless (Ananta), the eater of offerings (Hutabhuk), the enjoyer (Bhokta), the giver of happiness (Sukhada), born many times (Naikaja), the first-born (Agraja), never weary (Anirvinna), always patient (Sadamarshi), the support of the world (Lokadhishthana) and the wonderful (Adbhuta).

items.text:
सनात्सनातनतमः कपिलः कपिरव्ययः।
स्वस्तिदः स्वस्तिकृत्स्वस्ति स्वस्तिभुक्स्वस्तिदक्षिणः॥९६॥
items.tr:
sanātsanātanatamaḥ kapilaḥ kapiravyayaḥ|
svastidaḥ svastikṛtsvasti svastibhuksvastidakṣiṇaḥ||96||
items.en: He is the ancient (Sanat), the most ancient (Sanatanatama), the tawny sage (Kapila), the sun (Kapi), the undying (Avyaya), the giver of welfare (Svastida), the maker of welfare (Svastikrit), welfare itself (Svasti), the enjoyer of welfare (Svastibhuk) and the one skilled in giving welfare (Svastidakshina).

items.text:
अरौद्रः कुण्डली चक्री विक्रम्यूर्जितशासनः।
शब्दातिगः शब्दसहः शिशिरः शर्वरीकरः॥९७॥
items.tr:
araudraḥ kuṇḍalī cakrī vikramyūrjitaśāsanaḥ|
śabdātigaḥ śabdasahaḥ śiśiraḥ śarvarīkaraḥ||97||
items.en: He is not fierce (Araudra), wears earrings (Kundali), holds the discus (Chakri), is the valiant (Vikrami), of mighty command (Urjitashasana), beyond words (Shabdatiga), the one who bears all words (Shabdasaha), cool (Shishira) and the maker of night (Sharvarikara).

items.text:
अक्रूरः पेशलो दक्षो दक्षिणः क्षमिणांवरः।
विद्वत्तमो वीतभयः पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तनः॥९८॥
items.tr:
akrūraḥ peśalo dakṣo dakṣiṇaḥ kṣamiṇāṃvaraḥ|
vidvattamo vītabhayaḥ puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanaḥ||98||
items.en: He is not cruel (Akrura), gentle (Peshala), skilful (Daksha), generous (Dakshina), the best of the patient (Kshaminam Vara), the wisest (Vidvattama), free of fear (Vitabhaya) and the one whose story is holy to hear and sing (Punyashravanakirtana).

items.text:
उत्तारणो दुष्कृतिहा पुण्यो दुःस्वप्ननाशनः।
वीरहा रक्षणः सन्तो जीवनः पर्यवस्थितः॥९९॥
items.tr:
uttāraṇo duṣkṛtihā puṇyo duḥsvapnanāśanaḥ|
vīrahā rakṣaṇaḥ santo jīvanaḥ paryavasthitaḥ||99||
items.en: He lifts beings across (Uttarana), destroys evil deeds (Dushkritiha), is holy (Punya), the destroyer of bad dreams (Duhsvapnanashana), slayer of demon heroes (Viraha), the protector (Rakshana), the good (Santa), life (Jivana) and the one present everywhere (Paryavasthita).

items.text:
अनन्तरूपोऽनन्तश्रीर्जितमन्युर्भयापहः।
चतुरश्रो गभीरात्मा विदिशो व्यादिशो दिशः॥१००॥
items.tr:
anantarūpo'nantaśrīrjitamanyurbhayāpahaḥ|
caturaśro gabhīrātmā vidiśo vyādiśo diśaḥ||100||
items.en: He has endless forms (Anantarupa), endless glory (Anantashri), has conquered anger (Jitamanyu), removes fear (Bhayapaha), is the just one (Chaturashra), of deep nature (Gabhiratma), the one who gives various gifts (Vidisha), the one who gives commands (Vyadisha) and the one who directs (Disha).

items.text:
अनादिर्भूर्भुवो लक्ष्मीः सुवीरो रुचिराङ्गदः।
जननो जनजन्मादिर्भीमो भीमपराक्रमः॥१०१॥
items.tr:
anādirbhūrbhuvo lakṣmīḥ suvīro rucirāṅgadaḥ|
janano janajanmādirbhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ||101||
items.en: He has no beginning (Anadi), is the earth (Bhu), the support of the earth (Bhuva), Lakshmi (Lakshmi), the fine hero (Suvira), wearer of beautiful armlets (Ruchirangada), the begetter (Janana), the first cause of the birth of beings (Janajanmadi), the terrible (Bhima) and of terrible valour (Bhimaparakrama).

items.text:
आधारनिलयोऽधाता पुष्पहासः प्रजागरः।
ऊर्ध्वगः सत्पथाचारः प्राणदः प्रणवः पणः॥१०२॥
items.tr:
ādhāranilayo'dhātā puṣpahāsaḥ prajāgaraḥ|
ūrdhvagaḥ satpathācāraḥ prāṇadaḥ praṇavaḥ paṇaḥ||102||
items.en: He is the abode of the supports (Adharanilaya), has no maker (Adhata), smiles like a flower (Pushpahasa), is ever wakeful (Prajagara), goes upward (Urdhvaga), walks the good path (Satpathachara), gives life (Pranada), is the syllable Om (Pranava) and the one who rewards deeds (Pana).

items.text:
प्रमाणं प्राणनिलयः प्राणभृत्प्राणजीवनः।
तत्त्वं तत्त्वविदेकात्मा जन्ममृत्युजरातिगः॥१०३॥
items.tr:
pramāṇaṃ prāṇanilayaḥ prāṇabhṛtprāṇajīvanaḥ|
tattvaṃ tattvavidekātmā janmamṛtyujarātigaḥ||103||
items.en: He is the measure of truth (Pramana), the home of breath (Prananilaya), the sustainer of breath (Pranabhrit), the life of breath (Pranajivana), the reality (Tattva), the knower of reality (Tattvavid), the one Self (Ekatma) and the one beyond birth, death and old age (Janmamrityujaratiga).

items.text:
भूर्भुवःस्वस्तरुस्तारः सविता प्रपितामहः।
यज्ञो यज्ञपतिर्यज्वा यज्ञाङ्गो यज्ञवाहनः॥१०४॥
items.tr:
bhūrbhuvaḥsvastarustāraḥ savitā prapitāmahaḥ|
yajño yajñapatiryajvā yajñāṅgo yajñavāhanaḥ||104||
items.en: He is the tree of the three worlds (Bhurbhuvahsvastaru), the saviour (Tara), the begetter (Savita), the great-grandfather (Prapitamaha), the sacrifice (Yajna), lord of sacrifice (Yajnapati), the sacrificer (Yajva), whose limbs are the sacrifice (Yajnanga) and the one who carries the sacrifice (Yajnavahana).

items.text:
यज्ञभृद् यज्ञकृद् यज्ञी यज्ञभुक् यज्ञसाधनः।
यज्ञान्तकृद् यज्ञगुह्यमन्नमन्नाद एव च॥१०५॥
items.tr:
yajñabhṛd yajñakṛd yajñī yajñabhuk yajñasādhanaḥ|
yajñāntakṛd yajñaguhyamannamannāda eva ca||105||
items.en: He upholds the sacrifice (Yajnabhrit), makes the sacrifice (Yajnakrit), owns the sacrifice (Yajni), enjoys the sacrifice (Yajnabhuk), is the means of sacrifice (Yajnasadhana), completes the sacrifice (Yajnantakrit), the secret of sacrifice (Yajnaguhya), the food (Anna) and the eater of food (Annada).

items.text:
आत्मयोनिः स्वयंजातो वैखानः सामगायनः।
देवकीनन्दनः स्रष्टा क्षितीशः पापनाशनः॥१०६॥
items.tr:
ātmayoniḥ svayaṃjāto vaikhānaḥ sāmagāyanaḥ|
devakīnandanaḥ sraṣṭā kṣitīśaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ||106||
items.en: He is his own source (Atmayoni), self-born (Svayamjata), the one who dug the earth (Vaikhana), the singer of the Sama (Samagayana), the delight of Devaki (Devakinandana), the creator (Srashta), lord of the earth (Kshitisha) and the destroyer of sin (Papanashana).

items.text:
शङ्खभृन्नन्दकी चक्री शार्ङ्गधन्वा गदाधरः।
रथाङ्गपाणिरक्षोभ्यः सर्वप्रहरणायुधः॥१०७॥
items.tr:
śaṅkhabhṛnnandakī cakrī śārṅgadhanvā gadādharaḥ|
rathāṅgapāṇirakṣobhyaḥ sarvapraharaṇāyudhaḥ||107||
items.en: He holds the conch (Shankhabhrit), the sword Nandaka (Nandaki), the discus (Chakri), the bow Sharnga (Sharngadhanva) and the mace (Gadadhara); he has the wheel in his hand (Rathangapani), is unshakeable (Akshobhya) and has every kind of weapon (Sarvapraharanayudha).

items.text:
सर्वप्रहरणायुध ॐ नम इति।
वनमाली गदी शार्ङ्गी शङ्खी चक्री च नन्दकी।
श्रीमान् नारायणो विष्णुर्वासुदेवोऽभिरक्षतु॥१०८॥
items.tr:
sarvapraharaṇāyudha oṃ nama iti|
vanamālī gadī śārṅgī śaṅkhī cakrī ca nandakī|
śrīmān nārāyaṇo viṣṇurvāsudevo'bhirakṣatu||108||
items.en: 'He who has every kind of weapon: Om, salutation to him.' May the glorious Narayana, Vishnu, Vasudeva, who wears the forest garland and holds the mace, the bow Sharnga, the conch, the discus and the sword Nandaka, protect us.

items.text: श्रीवासुदेवोऽभिरक्षतु ॐ नम इति।
items.tr: śrīvāsudevo'bhirakṣatu oṃ nama iti|
items.en: 'May the glorious Vasudeva protect us: Om, salutation to him.'
